outcomes.original: Filing step: Commission an acoustic report and soundproofing plan from a licensed acoustical engineer, documenting existing conditions and proposing measures to contain noise, bass and vibrations within the building. What to say: The precedents show soundproofing is mandatory for any entertainment use in the Haight NCD with shared walls to residential units. The 2019 CUA at 1566 Haight required this condition verbatim, and the Planning Commission typically expects the acoustic plan to be part of the CUA application package.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Simultaneously with the CUA filing, submit the Place of Entertainment permit application to the Entertainment Commission, noting that Entertainment Commission approval is contingent on the Planning Commission CUA. What to say: The POE application should reference the pending CUA case number and state that the entertainment use will not commence until both the CUA and the POE permit are issued and all soundproofing conditions are met. Police Code Section 1060 requires a 30-day posted notice at the site and referrals to Police, Planning, DBI, DPH and Fire. The Entertainment Commission typically schedules hearings on the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays of the month, so coordinate timing with the Planning Commission CUA hearing (which takes 4-10 months). Filing the POE application early allows the referral agencies to review both applications together and ensures the Entertainment Commission hearing can be scheduled shortly after the Planning Commission acts.

Submit two sets of plans and allow 3-8 weeks for review. DPH charges $828-$2,207 depending on scope. outcomes.original: Filing step: If tenant improvements include structural, mechanical or electrical work, file a building permit application with DBI routed to Planning, DPH and other departments, and obtain all inspections and sign-offs before opening. What to say: The building permit application should include stamped architectural plans showing any layout changes, finishes, hood, HVAC, electrical panel upgrades, ADA compliance, and the soundproofing measures specified in the acoustic report. If the occupancy group changes (e.g., from B to A-2 because occupant load exceeds 50), the plans must document the change and show compliance with A-2 egress, fire protection and accessibility requirements. DBI routes the application to Planning for zoning review (the CUA satisfies this), DPH for health review (coordinate with the health plan check), and Fire for hood and assembly review. Obtain all final inspections and a certificate of final completion before the Entertainment Commission will allow operation under the POE permit.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 165 to 420 days. Estimated government cost: $6,578 to $21,200. Notes: The ranges cover the three approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120-300 days, $3,100-$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment permit (45-120 days, $2,708-$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), and Health Permit to Operate (14-45 days for health plan check plus 14-45 days for permit, $828-$2,500 plan check and $470-$1,000 permit per catalog:sf.health_plan_check and catalog:sf.health_permit). The CUA and POE permit applications can run in parallel but the POE hearing typically waits for the Planning Commission to act, so the total time is roughly the CUA timeline plus the POE timeline (not a simple sum). The comparable CUA cases took 4 to 424 days from filing to approval (N=2 approved), but one of those (1996.520C, 50 days) was decided in 1996 under different procedures; the 2019 CUA at 1566 Haight took 424 days. The cost range excludes building permit fees (which depend on construction valuation and whether a change of occupancy is triggered), ABC licence fees (unknown pathway), business registration, sign permit, FOG permit, state fees, music licensing, and professional services (architect, acoustic engineer, legal). These figures are times and costs to approval; they are not times or costs to a denial or withdrawal.
